newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan foreign car dealer sees record 96/97 sales.
newsitem.headline: Japan foreign car dealer sees record 96/97 sales.

text.p: Yanase & Co Ltd, a major Japanese dealer of foreign cars, expects sales to rise 13.8 percent from a year earlier to a record 87,520 cars in the 1996/97 business year, president Takahide Inayama said on Wednesday.
The previous sales record is 82,095 cars set in 1989/90.
Yanase sells General Motors (GM), Adam Opel AG and Mercedes-Benz cars in Japan.
Mercedes-Benz is a unit of Daimler-Benz AG. Adam Opel is GM's German unit.
Of the projected sales, Yanase expects to sell 46,000 Opel cars in 1996/97, up 16.5 percent from a year earlier, 31,920 Mercedes-Benz cars, up 11.7 percent, and 9,600 GM cars, up 8.8 percent.
Yanase sales of Mercedes-Benz cars account for nearly 80 percent of all sales of that vehicle in Japan and it accounts for nearly all of the Opel and GM cars sold here.
Inayama also said Yanase posted a current profit of 1.8 billion yen in 1995/96, the first profit in four years, helped by robust sales of Opel, Mercedes-Benz and GM cars.
Its current profit in 1996/97 is expected to hit 2.5 billion to 2.6 billion yen on sales of 460 billion yen, Inayama said.
Yanase is planning to invest 18 billion yen to open more Mercedes-Benz sales outlets. The number of outlets will increase to 100 by end-1997 from 31 as of end-1995.
Yanase is expected to introduce new Mercedes-Benz station wagons and coupes, and an Opel Vectra station wagon next year, Inayama said.
